decided.source: STAGE1_PLAN.md, section 9, 'Decisions taken during the build (step 3, 8 Nov)', decisions 11-13
decided.note: decided on reasons that do not depend on the gate's outcome; the results with the other choices stay recorded as evidence (here, and every panel run in reported_not_gated.plant_choices)

decisions.source: STAGE1_PLAN.md, section 9, 'Decisions taken during the build (step 3, 8 Nov)', decision 11
decisions.title: Ankle servo gains: joint space
decisions.reason: carpet.hold_servos defines one hold servo per joint for the screened model, which drives each ankle axis with one motor; applying that rule to each of the linkage's two motors doubles the ankle's joint-space stiffness, and half the gain per motor reproduces the screened stiffness exactly (the damping that results is in plant.json, gains.ankle_joint_space)

decisions.source: STAGE1_PLAN.md, section 9, 'Decisions taken during the build (step 3, 8 Nov)', decision 12
decisions.title: Ankle armature: the linkage's
decisions.reason: both motors' rotors are geared to both ankle axes, so each axis carries twice the screened single-motor armature: the physical two-motor ankle the plan specifies

decisions.source: STAGE1_PLAN.md, section 9, 'Decisions taken during the build (step 3, 8 Nov)', decision 13
decisions.title: G2 replay rule: a 20-start panel
decisions.reason: an open-loop replay has no feedback, so its fall time is chaotic (start offsets of 1 mm/s move one body's run from 25.8 to 5 strides); G2 is judged on the panel's median and the unperturbed run is reported

rules.panel: the median of 20 nominal replays with the envelope, from starts whose root velocity is offset in x and y by at most 1 mm/s (seed 0), is at least 10 strides (STAGE1_PLAN.md decision 13)
rules.single: the unperturbed nominal replay with the envelope walks at least 10 strides (plan section 3 step 3 as written)

Stage 1 transitions: starts, stops, speed changes and turn entries (``STAGE1_PLAN.md`` section 2, section 3
step 4, gate G3).

ankle_cap.rule: decision 15: each ankle's total torque command (feedforward, the servo's PD predicted from the encoders, the feedback) at most one motor's peak on each axis, and on a loaded foot no more than puts its CoP 5 mm inside its pad; the nearest such torque is commanded (control.cap_ankle_torque)
ankle_cap.residual: at every feedback update, the realised ankle torques (the ankle motors' forces in pitch and roll, G^T f) against decision 15's cap on the true state: an axis beyond one motor's peak, and a foot carrying more than 0.02 of the weight (its true load; also reported for 0.2, where R2's contact detection switches on) whose torques put its quasi-static CoP outside its pad's 5 mm inset, measured as the distance from the torques to the nearest torques that keep the CoP inside (N m; control.cap_ankle_torque); an excess over 1e-06 N m counts.  The check uses the loads and kinematics of the step the torques acted in; the cap had those of the step before (what the sensors give), so a load that changes within a step leaves a residual even for R1, which caps on the true joint state; R2 caps on its last sensor reading and pad-limits only the feet its estimator detects in contact

inward_bound.rule: decision 20: the swing pad, at its reference touchdown relative to the stance foot moved by the step offset, stays at least 5 mm from the stance pad (control.inward_room); the turn gap bounds nothing

clearance.rule: per swing, the inward bound at the reference touchdown (the swing pad at least 5 mm from the stance pad, decision 20); near touchdown (the given fractions of each swing) the swing foot moved inward by each delta and by the side's smallest bound through the swing leg's Jacobian; smallest distance, by the clearance screen's oracle, of the turning screen's pair (the turn gap), of the leg-to-leg pairs that only come close in motion, and of every leg-to-leg pair (capped)

turn_gap.note: the turning screen's turn gap is the pelvis plate's clearance to the same-side thigh in the turning pose, not a gap between the legs (decision 20)

estimator.stance_point: decision 19: the loaded pad's contact point (the mean of the foot's pad bottom corners within contact_tol_m of its lowest one)

falls.candidates: the hardware limits (HW_LIMITS) active at an update of the 0.5 s before the fall's onset (the last time the trunk tilt rose through 0.2 rad)
falls.attribution: STAGE1_PLAN.md decision 20: a condition that fails is body-limited by a hardware limit only if lifting that limit from the start (control.relaxed), over the condition's 20 starts (the same root-velocity offsets and noise seeds), improves survival significantly: a one-sided exact sign test on the paired survival times (strides to the fall; a run that does not fall outlasts one that does; two runs that do not fall tie; ties are dropped), p < 0.05.  The limits tested are the relaxable hardware limits that are candidates of at least one of the condition's falls (control.CANDIDATE_RULE); otherwise its falls are controller-limited.  The null, the same starts with the root velocity changed by a further 1 mm/s in x and nothing lifted, is reported as a chaos diagnostic and does not change the label.  Candidates the plant cannot lift (the CoP at a pad edge: the pads' size) are listed; lifting the candidates together is reported, not the label

stage1_sources.rule: sha256 over designlab/stage1/*.py in path order, each file as its path relative to the package, a NUL byte, its bytes and a NUL byte

earlier_defaults.note: G4 as the build first ran it, before decisions 15-20: the tracker at its earlier (untuned) defaults (control.EARLIER_DEFAULTS: heading 0.5 / 0.1, phase rate 2.0 / 1.0), no ankle cap, the inward step clamped at the turn gap less 1 mm, the estimator's stance odometry at the foot's centre of mass, every fall labelled by the episode-level counterfactual, judged on the unperturbed runs; kept as evidence (decision 17)
earlier_defaults.sources_rule: sha256 over designlab/stage1/*.py in path order, each file as its path relative to the package, a NUL byte, its bytes and a NUL byte

record.rule: R1 reproduces the design-study prototype: the nominal walk on hard floor at least 40 strides and at least 20 at friction 0.54; R2 at least 20 strides on the estimated CoM; each an unperturbed run from the reference's first frame (as the prototype ran), 60 strides long; the 20-start panels (G2's offsets) are reported beside the verdict

k_dcm.note: ankle: ZMP shift per unit DCM error (prototype)

cop_x.note: ankle: ZMP shift limit forward/back, m (prototype)

cop_y.note: ankle: ZMP shift limit sideways, m (prototype)

k_step.note: step: touchdown offset per unit DCM error (prototype)

step_out.note: step: offset limit outward, m (prototype; inward is the turn gap less 1 mm)

decay.note: step and heading offsets' decay over a stance (prototype)

d_trunk.note: trunk roll/pitch D, N m s/rad (prototype)

k_yaw.note: heading P: fraction of the stride-mean error corrected per step (prototype's value)

ki_yaw.note: heading I per step (a fifth of the P gain; chosen before any run)

k_phase.note: phase rate P, 1/m: 2 % per cm of forward DCM error (chosen before any run)

ki_phase.note: phase rate I, 1/(m s) (chosen before any run)

capture_margin.note: capture step: DCM distance outside the support that triggers it, m

turn_gap.note: the turn gap (the smaller of the target turns' smallest gaps) is between the trunk's pelvis and the same-side upper thigh, not between the legs (pair, leg_to_leg; lateral_gap_mm is the screen's leg-to-leg gap); the inward step clamp is kept as plan section 2 words it, pending the owner's choice of what bounds the inward step, and is the controller's own clip, not a hardware limit (inward_step_clearance: what moving the swing foot inward does to the turn gap's pair and to the leg-to-leg pairs)

inward_step_clearance.rule: near touchdown (the given fractions of each swing) the swing foot is moved inward by each delta through the swing leg's Jacobian; smallest distance, by the clearance screen's oracle, of the turning screen's pair (the turn gap), of the leg-to-leg pairs that only come close in motion, and of every leg-to-leg pair (capped)

noise.source: STAGE1_PLAN.md randomises IMU noise (section 2) without values; assumed MEMS-class figures: gyro white noise 0.003 rad/s per 2 ms sample (0.17 deg/s, about 0.011 deg/s/sqrt(Hz)) and a residual bias after a standstill calibration within +-2e-4 rad/s (about 40 deg/h); accelerometer 0.03 m/s^2 per sample (about 0.2 mg/sqrt(Hz)) and a bias within +-0.05 m/s^2; 14-bit absolute joint encoders; joint-rate noise 0.02 rad/s; foot-load noise 2 % of the weight

falls.rule: a hardware limit (HW_LIMITS) active at an update of the 0.5 s before the fall's onset is a candidate; it binds if the episode, restored to 1 s before the onset and continued with that limit relaxed, has not fallen and is upright (tilt below the onset's) 1 s after the original fall (a counterfactual): 'body-limited: <limits>' for the candidates whose relaxation alone does that, '... together' if only the candidates relaxed together do, else 'controller-limited'; 'undetermined' if the unchanged continuation does not repeat the fall or if a 1 mm/s change of the root velocity at the branch avoids it too (the fall is chaotic there); 'unconfirmed' if only a limit the plant cannot relax was a candidate
falls.replaces: the build's first rule: any limit (neck and tail drives and the turn-gap clamp included) active in 5 % of the window's updates, slip read from the foot body's own velocity (at its centre of mass above the pads); plan section 4 names the limits but not the test (the owner to confirm)
